title: Objective Filler Lexicon
description: Profile-organized vocabulary of DOMAIN-AGNOSTIC 'filler' tokens and vague-object phrasings that make a learning-objective statement vacuous or non-specific. A CO like 'Apply various techniques to solve real-world problems' is grammatically an objective but carries NO teachable skill signal once the Bloom verb ('apply') and this filler vocabulary ('various', 'techniques', 'real-world') are subtracted — nothing nameable remains. Consumed by (a) lib/objectives/filler_lexicon.py::filler_tokens, which subtracts these tokens from a statement's content-residual in the Defect-E cross-window lexical-dedup skill signature AND the Defect-B ObjectiveSpecificityValidator's V1 content-residual / V3 source-anchoring residual; and (b) lib/objectives/filler_lexicon.py::vague_object_regexes, which compiles the vague-object patterns the validator's V2 generic-object check keys on. Same profile discipline as semantik_lexicon.json / exercise_apparatus_lexicon.json (owner directive: publisher / subject vocabulary lives in data-driven lexicon PROFILES, never in code). The generic profile holds ONLY corpus-agnostic filler — a subject-specific term is never filler, so subject additions are EXTRA profiles, never edits to generic. The loader defaults to the UNION of every profile so no corpus-specific selection is baked into a call site.
$comment: Wave W2 (objective-synthesis fix plan, Defect B 'CO-statement specificity/vacuity gate' + Defect E filler-token subtraction). filler_tokens are lowercase single tokens matched after the statement is tokenized to [a-z]+ and stripped of Bloom verbs (lib/ontology/bloom.py::get_all_verbs) + generic stopwords (objective_dedup._SKILL_STOPWORDS); vague_object_patterns are phrase shapes (word-internal whitespace treated as \s+, matched case-insensitively, NOT word-boundary anchored) whose presence — combined with a thin content residual — marks a generic-object objective. A new subject / publisher is onboarded by adding a profile here, never by editing Python.

generic.description: Corpus-agnostic filler a mathematics / science / humanities objective uses regardless of subject: hedge quantifiers ('various', 'several'), empty nouns ('techniques', 'concepts', 'topics'), and evaluative adjectives ('effective', 'appropriate') that name no concrete skill object. NONE of these is ever a legitimate subject term, so subtracting them can only reveal — never hide — a real teachable skill.
